Container.Name: Polyfin-AIO
Container.Overview:
Polyfin is a self-hosted, Jellyfin-compatible media server for your own addons. It lets Jellyfin apps on TVs, phones and computers browse and play what your addons provide, with multiple users and transcoding.
EARLY DEVELOPMENT: Polyfin is not ready for everyday use yet.
ONE CONTAINER: this image runs its own PostgreSQL 18 database, in the folder postgresql of the Data folder. No PostgreSQL container is needed. The Data folder is required: without it, the database would be lost with the container. Make it writable by UID 65532 (chown 65532:65532 it in the terminal) before the first start.
FIRST RUN: open the container log and copy the one-time setup code, then open the WebUI and create the administrator with it. Afterwards the WebUI opens the web client, whose Dashboard opens Polyfin's admin page. Every option is set there, under Settings.
GPU (optional): Polyfin converts video on the first GPU that works and logs which one; Settings, Conversion chooses another. NVIDIA: install the Nvidia Driver plugin, add --runtime=nvidia to Extra Parameters, and set NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the GPU's UUID or all. AMD or Intel: add --device=/dev/dri to Extra Parameters.
BACKUPS: daily backups go to the Data folder by default, beside the database. Set Backups folder to another folder of the server, writable by UID 65532, then turn daily backups on in the admin page, under Settings, Backups.
STOPPING: Polyfin stops its database after itself. Extra Parameters give it a minute to do so; a container killed sooner recovers its database at the next start.
Polyfin hosts no content and ships with no addons or catalogues: you choose and configure your own sources. Do not forward its HTTP port to the internet.

Config.Name: HTTP port
Config.Description: Port for Jellyfin apps, the web client and the admin page. 8096 is the port Jellyfin apps try by default.

Config.Name: Discovery port
Config.Description: UDP port Jellyfin apps broadcast to when they look for servers on the local network. On the default bridge network, broadcasts do not reach the container: choose br0, which gives it its own address on your network, or Host, for apps to find Polyfin by themselves.

Config.Name: Data folder
Config.Description: Folder on the server for the database, the cache, and by default the recordings and backups, writable by UID 65532 (chown 65532:65532 it in the terminal). Required: the database lives here.

Config.Name: Secret key
Config.Description: Optional, advised: encrypts the API keys, client secret and tracking tokens Polyfin stores in the database. 32 random bytes in base64: run openssl rand -base64 32 in Unraid's terminal and paste the result. Keep a copy with your backups: with another key or none, the keys and connections have to be entered again.

Config.Name: NVIDIA GPUs
Config.Description: NVIDIA GPUs Polyfin may use, with --runtime=nvidia in Extra Parameters: all, or a GPU's UUID from the Nvidia Driver plugin.

Config.Name: NVIDIA capabilities
Config.Description: NVIDIA driver libraries the container gets. Video decoding and encoding need video; tone mapping HDR on the GPU needs graphics.

Config.Name: Recordings folder
Config.Description: Folder on the server Live TV recordings are written to, writable by UID 65532. Turn recording on in the admin page, under Settings, Recordings.

Config.Name: Backups folder
Config.Description: Folder on the server daily database backups are written to, writable by UID 65532, best on another disk than the Data folder. Turn backups on in the admin page, under Settings, Backups.
